In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the drowning of carbonate platforms on the Saharan margin during the Turonian-Senonian interval was controlled by both eustatic and tectonic factors.

the drowning of the Saharan carbonate platforms was induced by a combination of tectonics and climatic/oceanographic changes, the latter being probably responsible for the initial phase of drowning (mid-Turonien-early Coniacian) and the former being responsible for the final drowning (Coniacian-Santonien).

(i) carbonate platform development and drowning are controlled by the evolution of the margin, (ii) platform drowning is induced by a combination of tectonic, climatic and oceanographic factors, (iii) carbonate platforms are more sensitive to the evolution of their environment than to sea-level changes.

the sedimentologic and paleotetonic evolution of the African margin during the Turonian-Senonian was characterized by the development of carbonate platforms on the Saharan margin during the Turon-Senonian, and the drowning of these platforms during the Coniacian.

the evolution of carbonate platforms is strongly controlled by paleotectonic processes, which in turn are related to the segmentation of the passive margin by extensional faults.
